Implement InsertionMorphAction >### 3.18.0 >---------------------------- >- [feaLib] Fixed writing back nested glyph classes (1086). >- [TupleVariation] Reactivated shared points logic, bugfixes (1009). >- [AAT] Implemented ``morx`` ligature subtables (1082). >- [reverseContourPen] Keep duplicate lineTo following a moveTo (1080, > https://github.com/googlei18n/cu2qu/issues/51). >- [varLib.mutator] Suport instantiation of GPOS, GDEF and MVAR (1079). >- [sstruct] Fixed issue with ``unicode_literals`` and ``struct`` module in > old versions of python 2.7 (993). ### ufoLib 2.1.0 -> 2.1.1 >### 2.1.1 >- Clarify license, copyright and trademark strings for test fonts. They > now explicitly point to the license of the package (100). >- Ignore renameGlyphSet and deleteGlyphSet when formatVersion < 3 (91). >- Make fontLibValidator errors more verbose. ### ufo2ft 0.6.2 -> 1.1.0 >### 1.1.0 >- Read private 'useProductionNames' key from UFO lib. When this key is missing, it is implied to be True (same as the current default behavior): i.e. ``post`` glyph names are renamed based on ``public.postscriptNames`` if present, else ``uniXXXX`` names are auto-generated from the glyphs' ``unicode`` values. > If the key is set to False, then the ``post`` glyph names are not modified (186). >### 1.0.0 >- Added new `ufo2ft.featureWriters` package defining a new interface for generic feature writers. > Moved the two current default writers to the new package but temporarily kept the old modules as aliases. > The `ufo2ft.compile*` functions now also take a new `featureWriters` list of classes providing the same interface as BaseFeatureWriter, or also feature writer instances pre-loaded with custom options. >- [fontInfoData] Addded fallback for hhea `caretSlopeRise` and `caretSlopeRun` to match makeotf (177). >- [ufo2ft] Added `compileInterpolatableTTFs` function to create interpolatable TTFs using cu2qu algorithm. >- Added new `ufo2ft.filters` package for pre-processing UFO glyphs before compilation. Contains four filter implementations: "Decompose Components", "Remove Overlaps", "Cubic To Quadratic", and "Transformations". > Filters are specified with a special element in the UFO lib.plist. The key is "com.github.googlei18n.ufo2ft.filters", and the value is an array of plist dictionaries containing the filter "name", an optional "namespace" from which the filter module is to be imported from (the default is `"ufo2ft.filters"`), an array of "args" and a dict of "kwargs" which are passed on to the filter class's constructor, and finally either an "include" or an "exclude" array of glyph names to select the glyphs that are to be filtered. > The three core filters can also be toggled on/off with appropriate arguments to compileOTF/TTF functions, whereas the "Transformations" filter can only be specified via lib key. > The latter is intended to work in the same way as Glyphs.app's "Transformations" filter. However, currently it > only supports translate, scale and slant operatations. >- [ufo2ft] Added `reverseDirection=True` argument to compileTTF to optionally disable reversing path orientation when running cu2qu. >- [ufo2ft] Added `removeOverlaps=False` argument to compileOTF/TTF. Requires booleanOperations >= 0.7.1: > https://pypi.python.org/pypi/booleanOperations >- [ufo2ft] Added `inplace=False` argument to compileOTF/TTF. By default, the pre-processor copies the glyphs before applying any filters. If you don't care about the input font object being modified by compilation, you can use `inplace=True`. >- [ufo2ft] Removed deprecated `mtiFeaFiles` argument to compileOTF/TTF; the only supported way to compile MTI features is to embed them inside the UFO data folder. >- [outlineCompiler] Round head values that may be float in UFO (155). >- [outlineCompiler] Adds an empty zero-contour TTGlyph if the UFO glyph has invalid curveTo segments (e.g. `convertCubics` was set to False), and logs a warning instead of raising exception. ### brotli 0.6.0 -> 1.0.1 >### 1.0.1 >This is a source-only release. Binaries (except version) are the same > * updated `README.md` > * fixed parallel exeuction of CMake "compatibility" tests >### 1.0.0 > API changes > * new CLI; bro -> brotli; + man page > * remove "custom dictionary" support > * add ability to side-load brotli RFC dictionary > * add decoder API to avoid ringbuffer reallocation > * PY streaming decompression support > * PY wrapper accepts memview > New features > * C decoder (transpiled from Java) > * JS decoder (transpiled from Java) > * JNI wrappers > Improvements > * speedup Java decoder > * speedup compression of RLE-ish data That's it for now! Happy merging! 🤖

(`2734 > <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/2734>`_) >- Remove unnecessary mark evaluator in unittest plugin (`2767 > <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/2767>`_) >- Calls to ``Metafunc.addcall`` now emit a deprecation warning. This function > is scheduled to be removed in ``pytest-4.0``. (`2926 > <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/2926>`_) >### 3.2.4 >========================= >Bug Fixes >--------- >- Fix the bug where running with ``--pyargs`` will result in items with > empty ``parent.nodeid`` if run from a different root directory. (`2775 > <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/2775>`_) >- Fix issue with ``pytest.parametrize`` if argnames was specified as keyword arguments. > (`2819 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/2819>`_) >- Strip whitespace from marker names when reading them from INI config. (`1997 > <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1997>`_) >- Append example for pytest.param in the example/parametrize document. (`2658 > <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/2658>`_) >- Clarify language of proposal for fixtures parameters (`2893 > <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/2893>`_) >- List python 3.6 in the documented supported versions in the getting started > document. (`911 > <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/911>`_) ### fonttools 3.17.0 -> 3.21.0 >### 3.21.0 >---------------------------- >- [cmap] when compiling format6 subtable, don't assume gid0 is always called > '.notdef' (1e42224). >- [ot] Allow decompiling fonts with bad Coverage format number (1aafae8). >- Change FontTools licence to MIT (1127). >- [post] Prune extra names already in standard Mac set (df1e8c7). >- [subset] Delete empty SubrsIndex after subsetting (994, 1118). >- [varLib] Don't share points in cvar by default, as it currently fails on > some browsers (1113). >- [afmLib] Make poor old afmLib work on python3. >### 3.20.1 >---------------------------- >- [unicodedata] Fixed issue with ``script`` and ``script_extension`` functions > returning inconsistent short vs long names. They both return the short four- > letter script codes now. Added ``script_name`` and ``script_code`` functions > to look up the long human-readable script name from the script code, and > viceversa (1109, 1111). >### 3.20.0 >---------------------------- >- [unicodedata] Addded new module ``fontTools.unicodedata`` which exports the > same interface as the built-in ``unicodedata`` module, with the addition of > a few functions that are missing from the latter, such as ``script``, > ``script_extension`` and ``block``. Added a ``MetaTools/buildUCD.py`` script > to download and parse data files from the Unicode Character Database and > generate python modules containing lists of ranges and property values. >- [feaLib] Added ``__str__`` method to all ``ast`` elements (delegates to the > ``asFea`` method). >- [feaLib] ``Parser`` constructor now accepts a ``glyphNames`` iterable > instead of ``glyphMap`` dict. The latter still works but with a pending > deprecation warning (1104). >- [bezierTools] Added arc length calculation functions originally from > ``pens.perimeterPen`` module (1101). >- [varLib] Started generating STAT table (8af4309). Right now it just reflects > the axes, and even that with certain limitations: > * AxisOrdering is set to the order axes are defined, > * Name-table entries are not shared with fvar. >- [py23] Added backports for ``redirect_stdout`` and ``redirect_stderr`` > context managers (1097). >- [Graphite] Fixed some round-trip bugs (1093). >### 3.19.0 >---------------------------- >- [varLib] Try set of used points instead of all points when testing whether to > share points between tuples (1090). >- [CFF2] Fixed issue with reading/writing PrivateDict BlueValues to TTX file. > Read the commit message 8b02b5a and issue 1030 for more details. > NOTE: this change invalidates all the TTX files containing CFF2 tables > that where dumped with previous verisons of fonttools. > CFF2 Subr items can have values on the stack after the last operator, thus > a ``CFF2Subr`` class was added to accommodate this (1091). >- [_k_e_r_n] Fixed compilation of AAT kern version=1.0 tables (1089, 1094) >- [ttLib] Added getBestCmap() convenience method to TTFont class and cmap table > class that returns a preferred Unicode cmap subtable given a list of options > (1092). >- [morx] Emit more meaningful subtable flags. Implement InsertionMorphAction >### 3.18.0 >---------------------------- >- [feaLib] Fixed writing back nested glyph classes (1086). >- [TupleVariation] Reactivated shared points logic, bugfixes (1009). >- [AAT] Implemented ``morx`` ligature subtables (1082). >- [reverseContourPen] Keep duplicate lineTo following a moveTo (1080, > https://github.com/googlei18n/cu2qu/issues/51). >- [varLib.mutator] Suport instantiation of GPOS, GDEF and MVAR (1079). >- [sstruct] Fixed issue with ``unicode_literals`` and ``struct`` module in > old versions of python 2.7 (993). ### ufoLib 2.1.0 -> 2.1.1 >### 2.1.1 >- Clarify license, copyright and trademark strings for test fonts. They > now explicitly point to the license of the package (100). >- Ignore renameGlyphSet and deleteGlyphSet when formatVersion < 3 (91). >- Make fontLibValidator errors more verbose. ### ufo2ft 0.6.2 -> 1.1.0 >### 1.1.0 >- Read private 'useProductionNames' key from UFO lib. When this key is missing, it is implied to be True (same as the current default behavior): i.e. ``post`` glyph names are renamed based on ``public.postscriptNames`` if present, else ``uniXXXX`` names are auto-generated from the glyphs' ``unicode`` values. > If the key is set to False, then the ``post`` glyph names are not modified (186). >### 1.0.0 >- Added new `ufo2ft.featureWriters` package defining a new interface for generic feature writers. > Moved the two current default writers to the new package but temporarily kept the old modules as aliases. > The `ufo2ft.compile*` functions now also take a new `featureWriters` list of classes providing the same interface as BaseFeatureWriter, or also feature writer instances pre-loaded with custom options. >- [fontInfoData] Addded fallback for hhea `caretSlopeRise` and `caretSlopeRun` to match makeotf (177). >- [ufo2ft] Added `compileInterpolatableTTFs` function to create interpolatable TTFs using cu2qu algorithm. >- Added new `ufo2ft.filters` package for pre-processing UFO glyphs before compilation. Contains four filter implementations: "Decompose Components", "Remove Overlaps", "Cubic To Quadratic", and "Transformations". > Filters are specified with a special element in the UFO lib.plist. The key is "com.github.googlei18n.ufo2ft.filters", and the value is an array of plist dictionaries containing the filter "name", an optional "namespace" from which the filter module is to be imported from (the default is `"ufo2ft.filters"`), an array of "args" and a dict of "kwargs" which are passed on to the filter class's constructor, and finally either an "include" or an "exclude" array of glyph names to select the glyphs that are to be filtered. > The three core filters can also be toggled on/off with appropriate arguments to compileOTF/TTF functions, whereas the "Transformations" filter can only be specified via lib key. > The latter is intended to work in the same way as Glyphs.app's "Transformations" filter. However, currently it > only supports translate, scale and slant operatations. >- [ufo2ft] Added `reverseDirection=True` argument to compileTTF to optionally disable reversing path orientation when running cu2qu. >- [ufo2ft] Added `removeOverlaps=False` argument to compileOTF/TTF. Requires booleanOperations >= 0.7.1: > https://pypi.python.org/pypi/booleanOperations >- [ufo2ft] Added `inplace=False` argument to compileOTF/TTF. By default, the pre-processor copies the glyphs before applying any filters. If you don't care about the input font object being modified by compilation, you can use `inplace=True`. >- [ufo2ft] Removed deprecated `mtiFeaFiles` argument to compileOTF/TTF; the only supported way to compile MTI features is to embed them inside the UFO data folder. >- [outlineCompiler] Round head values that may be float in UFO (155). >- [outlineCompiler] Adds an empty zero-contour TTGlyph if the UFO glyph has invalid curveTo segments (e.g. `convertCubics` was set to False), and logs a warning instead of raising exception. ### brotli 0.6.0 -> 1.0.1 >### 1.0.1 >This is a source-only release. Binaries (except version) are the same > * updated `README.md` > * fixed parallel exeuction of CMake "compatibility" tests >### 1.0.0 > API changes > * new CLI; bro -> brotli; + man page > * remove "custom dictionary" support > * add ability to side-load brotli RFC dictionary > * add decoder API to avoid ringbuffer reallocation > * PY streaming decompression support > * PY wrapper accepts memview > New features > * C decoder (transpiled from Java) > * JS decoder (transpiled from Java) > * JNI wrappers > Improvements > * speedup Java decoder > * speedup compression of RLE-ish data That's it for now! Happy merging! 🤖

pull_request.title: Possible Contribution to JUNG
pull_request.body:
This is my current JUNG visualization and samples code. It has an R-Tree and R*-Tree in use for Nodes and Edges. The RTree.java class has a link to a paper that describes how they work.
This code also changes all V to N, Vertex to Node, and Transformer to Function. All Applet references are also gone.

Let me know what you think and we can discuss this as a contribution to JUNG.

Cheers.
Tom Nelson

issue.title: Possibility to use in a gnome shell extension?
issue.body:
Hi,

being a hobby developer of a gnome shell extension I always felt a bit uneasy in the gjs ecosystem compared to nodejs. So naturally this project looks very promising to me.

Specifically I now need third-party nodejs libraries in my gnome shell extension.

I wondered, would it be possible to build up the node js environment in a gnome shell extension?

comment.body:
> would it be possible to build up the node js environment in a gnome shell extension?

the goal of this project is to give you access to common NodeJS core modules (incomplete, work in progress) and provide CommonJS hooks to be able to `require('./file')` or `require('module')` via `package.json` so you can use `npm` via GJS too.

However, it's very hard to bring the whole NodeJS env in GJS because hooks with libuv and the rest of the node is missing.

That being said, every core module is being implemented as "best use case" or "best common need" so if there's something in particular you need either push a PR for the right core module or file a bug if something is not working as expected.

Did this answer your question?

issue.title: GT Cables and Wire don't not connect EIO RF conduits
issue.body:
##### Versions:

- Gregtech 5.09.31

##### Issue Description:

An EnderIO RF conduit does not create connectors to a GT Cable or Wire converting EU to RF.
Although RF are properly inserted into the RF conduit .
Missing connectors prevents controlling the connexion (example disable unwanted)
Connexion is not visually enabled although RF transfer occurs.

![2017-12-31_18 51 28](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1111474/34463444-7439a442-ee5c-11e7-8763-ccd44e97d50e.png)

comment.body:
> All wires and pipes are pipes, technically.

- Gregtech Item Pipes correctly advertises themselves as Item containers and causes EnderIO to enable a connector with Item Conduits only.
- Gregtech Fluid Pipes correctly advertises themselves as Fluid containers and causes EnderIO to enable a connector with Fluid Conduits only.
- Gregtech Energy Pipes (Cables and Wires) wrongly advertises themselves as Fluid containers and, causes EnderIO to enable a connector with Fluid Conduits instead of Energy Conduits.

> Won't be fixed by GT because… as its visual it's not really an issue.

#####  Consequences are not only visual, but affect conduit behaviour, ability to control RF transfers and can cause unnecessary ticking load.

- EnderIO Energy Conduit will get injected RF from Gregtech Cables and Wires regardless of unavailable options, since there is no connector to access conduit connection settings. It is so impossible to decide of connexion status, or direction of energy transfer that is needed when RF to EU conversion is enabled.
- EnderIO Fluid Conduits are mislead by Gregtech Cables and Wires to enable a connector, ticking useless impossible fluid transfer attempts with Gregtech Cables and Wires, unless each wrong connector is individually disabled.

##### Reasons to review this glitch:

Gregtech Pipes had recent changes to their connexion mechanic.
While reviewing and debugging these pull requests:
- Fixing how Cables and Wires advertises themselves (changing from Fluid Container to RF Energy Emitters and Acceptors instead) sounds just appropriate when attention is focussed on relevant Gregtech code portions.

issue.title: Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'upload' of undefined

milestone.description: UI enhancements

issue.body:
This happens only when chunk is enabled, on S3 mode.

```
        chunking: {
            enabled: true,
            concurrent: { enabled: true }
        },
```

Turn on debug mode, then try to upload a big file, then disconnect wifi in the middle.  Wait for a bit, until 3 retries are over.

Then, there will be an error:

 Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'upload' of undefineds3.jquery.fine-uploader.js:5594 qq.extend._registerProgressHandlers3.jquery.fine-uploader.js:9434 chunked.put.chunked.initHeaders.then.promise.failure.errors3.jquery.fine-uploader.js:1109 (anonymous function)s3.jquery.fine-uploader.js:659 qq.eachs3.jquery.fine-uploader.js:1108 qq.extend.successs3.jquery.fine-uploader.js:9418 (anonymous function)s3.jquery.fine-uploader.js:1109 (anonymous function)s3.jquery.fine-uploader.js:659 qq.eachs3.jquery.fine-uploader.js:1108 qq.extend.successs3.jquery.fine-uploader.js:8494 handleSignatureReceiveds3.jquery.fine-uploader.js:3804 onCompletes3.jquery.fine-uploader.js:3909 (anonymous function)

I've investigated a bit on this...

On line 5560, this gets called: _registerProgressHandler()
On line 5561, it will try to use the handler to get xhr.  Unfortunately, it fails to get the xhr.
On line 5594, without checking xhr variable, it tries to assign a new function on top of xhr.upload, and boom, "Cannot read property 'upload'".

I advise to resolve the issue by making a check right before definition of the function.

Something like...

```
        if( xhr === undefined )
            xhr = {};

        if( xhr.upload === undefined )
            xhr.upload = {};
```
# 

Btw, I do notice that while most of the time this happens, everyone once a while this does not.  I'm not sure about the whole flow of the code, or how the threading works here, but yeah, that's how I see the bug currently.

Last but not least I thought this whole fineuploader thing was really well made.  Really love it a lot. 

Thanks guys!

Cheers,
Thomas

pull_request.title: Implement extensible syscall interface for wasm
pull_request.body:
This needs tests before it can be merged, but I decided to open a PR now to get feedback on the approach.

Currently it's possible to run tests with the native wasm target, but it's not possible to tell whether they pass or to capture the output, because libstd throws away stdout, stderr and the exit code. While advanced libstd features should probably require more specific targets (eg. wasm-unknown-web) I think even the unknown target should at least support basic I/O.

Any solution is constrained by these factors:
- It must not be javascript specific
- There must not be too strong coupling between libstd and the host environment (because it's an "unknown" target)
- WebAssembly does not allow "optional" imports - all imports *must* be resolved.
- WebAssembly does not support calling the host environment through any channel *other* than imports.

The best solution I could find to these constraints was to give libstd a single required import, and implement a syscall-style interface through that import. Each syscall is designed such that a no-op implementation gives the most reasonable fallback behaviour. This means that the following import table would be perfectly valid:
```javascript
imports.env = { rust_wasm_syscall: function(index, data) {} }
```

Currently I have implemented these system calls:
- Read from stdin
- Write to stdout/stderr
- Set the exit code
- Get command line arguments
- Get environment variable
- Set environment variable

It need not be extended beyond this set if being able to run tests for this target is the only goal.

issue.title: `return` assignment with escaped value incorrectly eliminated
issue.body:
Something like this:

```coffeescript
foo: ->
  bar = null
  callback = =>
    bar._currentCount = @_count++
  bar = something(callback)
```

Produces correct code in `3.2.*`:

```javascript
{var a,l
return a=null,l=(t=>(a._currentCount=this._count++)),a=something(l)}
```

However in `3.3.*`:

```javascript
{var a,l
return a=null,l=(t=>(a._currentCount=this._count++)),something(l)}
```

issue.title: Libc stdio file descriptors not reserved
issue.body: When a libc component is started and stdin, stdout, or stderr are configured the descriptors 1, 2, and 3 are assigned like any other Unix environment. But if any are not configured, the descriptor gap is used for normal files or the stdio descriptors become misaligned. This currently causes problems with the Nim asynchronous event dispatcher, and is a potential source of confusion elsewhere.

issue.title: G28 Z-Homing Broken for Me with 1.1.x Release Branch
issue.body:
My printer is a Prusa i3 clone utilizing MKS GEN 1.2 electronics (functional RAMPS 1.3 clone) with an inductive sensor for Z homing and Linear ABL. I've used this configuration for some time with great results running 1.1 RC7 & RC8. However, any code in the 1.1.x release branch (tried 1.1.0, 1.1.0-1, 1.1.1, 1,1,2 & 1.1.3) has a problem when running G28 to home all axes. Using the release code, the G28 appears to execute correctly, but upon completion, after the nozzle/probe raises to 10mm + my M851 offset, the LCD properly displays this Z height while Repetier Host 1.6.2 only shows the Z height to be the M851 offset without the 10mm safety raise. The LCD also displays the message "Endstops Z" at the end of the G28. After this, there is nothing I can do to synchronize the Z-height in Repetier to the actual Z-height properly displayed on the LCD.  As a result, I'm unable to manually move the nozzle below 10mm in Repetier using the 1.1.x release branch. I've spent a lot of time trying to isolate the problem without success. If I revert to RC8, all is once again well.

I enabled debugging for autoleveling in both RC8 and 1.1.1 and I've attached the debug output of a G28 command for each version, as well as a copy of my Configuration.h. My settings are always manually crossed-over between versions to avoid any variable name conflicts and I can't for the life of me see any configuration setting(s) that would lead to this behavior. Also use M502/M500 after flashing to account for varying settings sizes between RC8 & the release code.

Any help would be greatly appreciated, for I am stumped and stuck on RC8.

Thanks,
Kevin

[1-1-1 G28 Debug.txt](https://github.com/MarlinFirmware/Marlin/files/1082450/1-1-1.G28.Debug.txt)

[Configuration.h.txt](https://github.com/MarlinFirmware/Marlin/files/1082455/Configuration.h.txt)

# Tasks

[![Build Status](https://scrutinizer-ci.com/g/owncloud/tasks/badges/build.png?b=master)](https://scrutinizer-ci.com/g/owncloud/tasks/build-status/master) [![Scrutinizer Code Quality](https://scrutinizer-ci.com/g/owncloud/tasks/badges/quality-score.png?b=master)](https://scrutinizer-ci.com/g/owncloud/tasks/?branch=master) [![Code Coverage](https://scrutinizer-ci.com/g/owncloud/tasks/badges/coverage.png?b=master)](https://scrutinizer-ci.com/g/owncloud/tasks/?branch=master)

Tasks app for ownCloud.

### Installation

 * **Using git:** In your `owncloud/apps/` directory, run `git clone https://github.com/owncloud/tasks/`. Then go to the Apps manager tab in your Owncloud web interface, and enable the Tasks app.
 * **Using the zip archive:** Download the latest [zip archive](https://github.com/owncloud/tasks/archive/master.zip), extract the `tasks-master` directory inside your `owncloud/apps/` directory, and rename it to `tasks`. For stable releases, you can also download one of the [releases](https://github.com/owncloud/tasks/releases) tar.gz archives. Then go to the Apps manager tab in your Owncloud web interface, and enable the Tasks app.
 
### Usage/Features

Once enabled, a new `Tasks` menu will appear in your owncloud apps menu. From there you can **add and delete tasks, edit their title, description,  start and due dates, reminder times, mark them as important, and add comments on them**. Tasks can be **shared** between users. Tasks can be **synchronized using CalDav** (each task list is linked to an Owncloud calendar, to sync it to your local client - Thunderbird, Evolution, KDE Kontact, iCal... - just add the calendar as a remote calendar in you client). You can **download your tasks as ICS** files using the download button for each calendar.

### Screenshot

![tasks](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/2496460/9783697/ab337634-57a6-11e5-9633-b8f950b1e28e.png)

pull_request.title: LED Blink
pull_request.body:
This is a simple project to make an LED repetitively blink.

Requires: x1 Arduino Board, x1 Breadboard, x1 5mm LED Light, x2 Jumper Wires, x1 220, 1K, or 10K resistor.

Steps:
1. Place the positive jumper wire into digital port 13, with the other end being in the positive node of the breadboard.
2. Place the negative jumper wire into digital port GND, with the other end being in the negative node of the breadboard.
3. Place your LED with the positive wire being in the main area of the breadboard, and the negative wire on the negative node of the breadboard.
4. Place your transistor on the positive node of the breadboard, with the other end being in the same row as your LED. Be sure not to make them touch!
5. Plug in your Arduino and run the program.

It supports socket methods like `setsockopts()`, but > prohibits `send()`, `recv()`, `close()` and any other calls that > can interfere with the transport that ultimately owns this file > descriptor. >* `TCP_NODELAY` is used by default for all TCP connections. >* Make `Transport.resume_reading()` and `pause_reading()` idempotent. > This will match asyncio in Python 3.7. Issue 93. >* `loop.create_server()` keeps a strong reference to the `Server` > object it returns until its closed. Fixes 81. >* Fix `loop.connect_accepted_socket()` to return correct SSL > transport. >* The UDP transport layer was rewritten from scratch. Now it uses > `uv_poll_*` libuv APIs, instead of high-level `uv_udp_*` ones. > This could mean a slight performance regression, and will be > reverted when we port uvloop to Windows. For now this is > the only viable option to make uvloop fully compatible with asyncio. > When libuv gets an API to connect UDP sockets, `uv_udp_connect()`, > we'll be able to switch to a better UDP implementation. Issue 109. >* `UDPTransport.sendto(data, addr)` will raise an exception if > `addr` requires a name resolution. Issue 91. > Low-level sockets >* `loop.add_reader()` and `loop.add_writer()` accept file-like > objects. Issue 97. >* `loop.sock_connect()` supports 4 element address tuples for > IPv6 sockets. Issue 99. >* Protect sockets from closing while they are in use by > `loop.sock_*()` methods. Close all reader/writer sockets the > loop owns when it closes. Issue 100. > Other event loop APIs >* `loop.run_until_complete()` cleans up done callbacks in all > situations. By jimmylai. > See also Python issue: https://bugs.python.org/issue30423. >* New `uv_loop_fork()` libuv API is used in `loop.subprocess_shell()` > and `loop.subprocess_exec()` making them more stable. Issue 39. >* `loop.call_later()` accepts infinite time `float('inf')`. > Issue 102. >* `loop.subprocess_exec()` accepts `pathlib.Path` objects for its > `cwd` parameter. Issue 90. >* Support `pathlib.Path` objects in `loop.create_unix_connection()` > and `loop.create_unix_server()`. >* Try removing existing stale Unix socket paths in > `loop.create_unix_server()`. >* `ascii` encoding is tried before encoding with `idna`. > Issue 95. >* Fix `slow_callback_duration` repr in warnings for callback handles > and Tasks. Issue 110. > Miscellaneous >* Drop custom uvloop Future and Task implementations. Aside > from bug fixes and performance improvements, libuv survives > `fork`. >* `LIBUV_CONFIGURE_HOST` environment variable can be used to > cross-compile uvloop/libuv. By cmcqueen, for issue 104. >* Cyhton was upgraded from 0.25.2 to 0.27.3. >* uvloop binary is linked with `pthread`. issue.title: Can't use SSL behind nginx reverse proxy
issue.body:
Discovered my own workaround, but if the container is running behind nginx serving up the SSL certificate, it is not aware it is using an SSL cert and writes all stylesheets and form elements using http://. Browsers disable mixed content, so it shows it with no styles.

Workaround for me was to make is_ssl() in wp-includes/load.php always return true.

## Changelogs ### uvloop 0.8.1 -> 0.9.1 >### 0.9.1 >* Stop using malloc for `uv_request*` handlers. >* Fix `loop.add_reader()`, `loop.add_writer()`, `loop.remove_reader()`, > and `loop.remove_writer()` to better track socket objects. >* Fix `loop.sock_recv()`, `loop.sock_sendall()`, `loop.sock_recv_into()`, > and `loop.sock_connect()` to correctly handle `Task.cancel()`. >* Better handle immediate cancellation of `loop.create_connection()`. >* Make unit tests stricter: ensure `loop.call_exception_handler()` > does not get called, unless it's expected. >### 0.9.0 > TCP & UDP >* `transport.get_extra_info('socket')` now returns a socket-like > object. It supports socket methods like `setsockopts()`, but > prohibits `send()`, `recv()`, `close()` and any other calls that > can interfere with the transport that ultimately owns this file > descriptor. >* `TCP_NODELAY` is used by default for all TCP connections. >* Make `Transport.resume_reading()` and `pause_reading()` idempotent. > This will match asyncio in Python 3.7. Issue 93. >* `loop.create_server()` keeps a strong reference to the `Server` > object it returns until its closed. Fixes 81. >* Fix `loop.connect_accepted_socket()` to return correct SSL > transport. >* The UDP transport layer was rewritten from scratch. Now it uses > `uv_poll_*` libuv APIs, instead of high-level `uv_udp_*` ones. > This could mean a slight performance regression, and will be > reverted when we port uvloop to Windows. For now this is > the only viable option to make uvloop fully compatible with asyncio. > When libuv gets an API to connect UDP sockets, `uv_udp_connect()`, > we'll be able to switch to a better UDP implementation. Issue 109. >* `UDPTransport.sendto(data, addr)` will raise an exception if > `addr` requires a name resolution. Issue 91. > Low-level sockets >* `loop.add_reader()` and `loop.add_writer()` accept file-like > objects. Issue 97. >* `loop.sock_connect()` supports 4 element address tuples for > IPv6 sockets. Issue 99. >* Protect sockets from closing while they are in use by > `loop.sock_*()` methods. Close all reader/writer sockets the > loop owns when it closes. Issue 100. > Other event loop APIs >* `loop.run_until_complete()` cleans up done callbacks in all > situations. By jimmylai. > See also Python issue: https://bugs.python.org/issue30423. >* New `uv_loop_fork()` libuv API is used in `loop.subprocess_shell()` > and `loop.subprocess_exec()` making them more stable. Issue 39. >* `loop.call_later()` accepts infinite time `float('inf')`. > Issue 102. >* `loop.subprocess_exec()` accepts `pathlib.Path` objects for its > `cwd` parameter. Issue 90. >* Support `pathlib.Path` objects in `loop.create_unix_connection()` > and `loop.create_unix_server()`. >* Try removing existing stale Unix socket paths in > `loop.create_unix_server()`. >* `ascii` encoding is tried before encoding with `idna`. > Issue 95. >* Fix `slow_callback_duration` repr in warnings for callback handles > and Tasks. Issue 103. > Python 3.7 >Some APIs that will be available in Python 3.7 in vanilla asyncio, >but can be used with uvloop today. >* Implement `.cancelled()` method for callback and timer handles. >* Add `Transport.is_reading()`. >* Implement `loop.sock_recv_into()`. >* Python 3.7.0a1 is now supported. Issue 110. > Miscellaneous >* Drop custom uvloop Future and Task implementations. This means > that there will be a tiny performance regression for Python 3.5 > deploys. >* Limit stack traces in debug mode to make it faster. >* `signal.siginterrupt` is now used by signals machinery to let > system calls to be repeated by default, instead of raising an > `EINTR`. > Build >* libuv in uvloop has been upgraded from v1.11.0 to v1.17.0. Aside > from bug fixes and performance improvements, libuv survives > `fork`. >* `LIBUV_CONFIGURE_HOST` environment variable can be used to > cross-compile uvloop/libuv. By cmcqueen, for issue 104. >* Cyhton was upgraded from 0.25.2 to 0.27.3. >* uvloop binary is linked with `pthread`. issue.title: AI: add Lua function ai.get_individual_attacks()
issue.body:
Migrated from the EasyCoding wiki page:

Add a Lua function ai.get_individual_attacks() that returns all the single attacks the side can do (as opposed to attack combinations).  This needs to include an option to recalculate and take the current situation on the map into account (making the function believe that the game state has changed).

comment.body:
Indeed.  With the slight correction that it is `ai.get_attacks` which provides this information, it's all there. Not sure for how long this has been hanging around on the EasyCoding page ...

In any case, closing this issue.

issue.title: Weight normalization for RNN Cells.
issue.body:
The current RNN implementation executes a user defined
function (the call() method of subclasses of RNNCells) inside a
tf.while() loop. Weight normalisation requires a one-time
 normalization of the transition matrices prior to
entering the while loop. The following 2 edits have been made in
tensorflow/python/ops to enable this functionality:

 - RNNCell now has a prepare() method. It does nothing as implemented
in the base class
 - A call to cell.prepare() has been added just before entering
 _dynamic_rnn_loop()

Subclasses of RNNCell may implement normalization in the cell's
prepare() method. One implementation with BasicLSTMCell
and associated tests have been added to contrib. Note that any
wrappers to be used with a weight-normalized cell need to be
appropriately subclassed, as illustrated with the
PrepareableMultiRNNCell example in contrib.

Presently (Jan 2018) config.yml and docker-compose.yml use hard-coded user:password credentials, in real world deployment this should use some abstraction layer.  Examples of secure mechanisms for this would be docker_login or some external call to a AS in your infrastructure ((open)ldap,krb5,saml) that would be defined in an auth or environment variable.

As an example there is a stub file ( `auth_keys_from_cas` ) in this repo that could be used as a file that would have the hashed/encrypted values for tokens/user:pass entries for all auth'd users.

	Example deployment using such a file:
	* 	User authenticates to local domain/AS server
	*	Server passes (over secure channel communication (DTLS or other secure channel within organization's policies) to this file not much unlike a journal write of a auth attempt for admin/sudo rights.
	*	Config.yml calls this file to populate auth'd hosts/users and timeout periods of said tokens (if used), to populate it's auth'd user db or update it on some on-demand or periodic schedule.
```

issue.title: Radio button and checkboxes not accepting .form-check class on mobile device
issue.body:
Device noted on:
Motorola Z2 force, with Nougat 8.0. (recently upgraded.)

Expected behavior: left padding/margin styling. 
Current behavior: radios and checkboxes are to the extreme left and cutoff partially.

So I tested this and it definitely has something to do with the .form-check class. Apparently when you add form-check it is supposed to push the radio button and checkbox to the right, and then the form-check-input is supposed to correct the padding by applying the opposite padding amount to the left to zero it out to even.

As it stands, on the moto z2 force, only the form-check-input is being added to the dom, and thus it is pushing the radio and checkboxes off of the screen to the left since it is basically applying it's padding without form-checks padding to counteract it. Not sure if this is just with this phone or not, but once I remove those classes the radio buttons line up properly. 

Incidentally, form-check works properly on other form elements. Only the radio and checkboxes seem affected at this point.

issue.title: could Roentgenium fit on a floppy?
issue.body:
Even today the floppies are still being used, for example - as virtual floppies inside the coreboot open source BIOS. Just imagine: your wonderful OS could be a part of someone's BIOS build! _(for coreboot supported motherboard, maybe you have or could get one - see https://www.coreboot.org/Supported_Motherboards )_

If you already have a coreboot-supported motherboard, or a real chance to get one, - wouldn't it be cool to be able to launch your own OS straight from the BIOS chip? ;) With one simple command its possible to add any floppy to coreboot BIOS build - and then you see it as a boot entry! Multiple floppies could be added this way _(as long as you have enough space left inside the BIOS flash chip, luckily LZMA compression could be used for the stored floppies to reduce their occupied size)_

issue.title: Issue with Collections
issue.body:
I have a form, which model is defined like that:
`<Form model="forms.reservation.trips[0]" />`

and control in it, which model is defined like that:
`<Control.text model=".passengersNumber" />`

and I have a submit button, like that:
`<Button type="submit" />`

When I hit the submit button, a Redux action is dispatched, which looks like that:
```
{
  type: 'rrf/addIntent',
  model: 'forms.reservation.trips[0]',
  intent: {
    type: 'submit'
  }
}
```

I then expect an action like that to be triggered,
```
{
  type: 'rrf/setSubmitFailed',
  model: 'forms.reservation.trips[0]',
  submitFailed: true,
  clearIntents: {
    type: 'submit'
  }
}
```

However, nothing is triggered. I think the problem is at form-component.js - handleIntents() function. formValue is getting a value of "forms.reservation.trips", instead of forms.reservation.trips[0].  So the code is looking for intents changes at forms.forms.reservation.trips.$form.intents. However the rrf/addIntent action added the intent to forms.forms.reservation.trips[0].$form.intents.

Am I doing something wrong, or this is actual bug with the library?

5. You can open the redux console and hit the Continue to Next Step button. You will see the rrf/addIntent action is dispatched, but not and the rrf/setSubmitFailed.

Regards

commits.message:
Move PlaybackDto.toRes() to PlaybackRes

The convention is to move transformation methods close to their target
class, because that's the location where it will most likely be used.
toRes() was a member method of PlaybackDto for some reason.

Remove unnecessary safe-call

currentUser() cannot return null according to its signature. This caused
a warning.

Add json column for artists to RawPlaybackData

RawPlaybackData has an element collection for the artists. Due to
Hibernate being a serious clusterfuck, it is pretty hard to aggregate
playbacks over an element collection, or merely selecting it for that
matter. It mostly generates illegal SQL queries instead of complaining.

To simplify things, we add another redundant column "artist_json", which
simply contains a json encoded string list with all artists. Whether we
get rid of the element collection later is yet to be decideed. For the
time being, one can simply decide which one to use for queries, at the
acceptable cost of maintaining the redundant column.

Add endpoint to retrieve broken playbacks accumulated

This commit adds a new endpoint under .../playbacks/acc. The endpoint
can be used to retrieve broken playbacks in an accumulated fashion. That
is, an identical playback (same artists/title/release) that occurs n
times makes only *one* entry in the result set, whose "occurrences"
field is n. Moreover, the result set is sorted by occurrences. This
endpoint might be quite useful to retrieve broken playbacks that are
useful to fix.

Accordingly, we might offer an endpoint to "bulk-fix" such identical
playbacks soon.
Update .gitignore to ignore cover_db of Devel::Cover

Sort configuration options alphabetically

That's the only way we'll keep overview when the options list grows.

Fix encoding bug for json formatter

encode_json() produces a raw byte string, but the IO layer is not aware
that this is utf8. That caused issues in the json formatter. We now
manually set the utf8 flag for those strings which is accurate when
using utf8 io layer.

Use JSON::MaybeXS everywhere

Faster if XS is available, but works without as well.

Show accumulated broken playbacks

This patch enables the client to display data from the .../playbacks/acc
endpoint. This endpoint provides broken playbacks accumulated by their
values of artists/title/release. The result set is sorted by occurences,
i.e. if a single (broken) track has been played often, it will appear on
the top of this list. The returned accumulation is a good indicator as
to what playbacks should be fixed to reduce the number of broken ones
the most.
The data can be obtained by using the list command with the --acc flag.
All supported formatters are able to display the result set, with the
limitation that CSV only shows the first artist.

issue.title: Allow index settings in Meta.index
issue.body:
Currently, when defining a new `DocType` you have to create a separate `Index` object if you wish to configure any index-level settings. With the deprecation of multiple types in elasticsearch 6.0 it might make more sense to just allow the index settings to configurable on the `DocType` itself in some fashion.

This would then allow even for situations where given `DocType` is present in multiple indices (time-based indices for example) meaning its `Meta.index` would specify a wildcard (`products-*` for example) and provide settings which would then allow it to generate and save an `IndeTemplate` and/or create any particular index via the `init` classmethod.

Any ideas and feedback is more than welcome!

issue.title: Playervault open item
issue.body:
This feature adds the option to open the PVX


Some servers (like mine) have playervault set up in a way where they can only be accessed through the PV sign. This means that the player has to go to the designated area, where the PV signs are, to open a vault.

 This feature will allow players to open their PV with this item regardless of where they are. PVX will give the player this item* which they will hold in their hand. The player will then right click with the item in hand. PVX will then remove the item* and then open the PV GUI, where the player can pick which vault to open.

I don't think I need to elaborate on the GUI; from the discord server, I think we all have a good idea how the GUI will function.

*ITEM
This item should have settings in config.yml. i would like the ability to set:
- material_name or item_name 
- item_data
- name of the item
- lore lines
- Endless item**
- Enchant on the item
- message when item is successfully consumed
- a cooldown time between using this item 2 times in a row
- Region/World blacklist to deny using this item

** Endless item means there is a version of this item which has unlimited uses; the item should remain in the inventory even after the player has used it. This should not be a default option. 

There should be an argument where the server owner can specify if they want the item to be endless or not.

I know you are asking yourself "Why add endles version?? It is the damn thing as using the command". So, with the idea of opening PVs using signs only, having this item would be somewhat rare, and people should be able to get it if another player dies, or drops it, etc. 

-----

Settings example:


PVItem:
  Material: 'stick'
  Data: 0
  Enchants:
    - '34:10' # unbreaking 10
    - 'silk_touch:1' #idk why someone would use 2 enchants but the option should be there anyways
  CustomName: "&c&lplayervault express"
  Lore:
    - 'lore line 1'
    - 'lore line X'
  onOpenMessage: "(cool server) you opened the vaults"
  onCloseMessage: "(hot server) you close the vaults"

-----
Commands example, <required> [optional]

/pv giveitem <player> <amount> <Endless? (True/false>
  > /pv giveitem Flavour 1 true - gives endless item
  > /pv giveitem Flavour 1 false - gives consumable
  
--
I know i probably don't need to say it, but for server with 99 vaults, there would need to be pages in the GUI. Pages means there will need to be buttons like Next, Last, close, etc. I wanted to say that these should customizable so we can manipulate the GUI how we want it. Basically let us choose what buttons go where (or if we want to disable a button type)

While I am working on this I have some second thoughts: the current data-layer middleware design is great in a way that hides itself from components that dispatch the action. issue.title: Move hydrate from core to userland 🚰
issue.body:
Why not start 2018 off right by losing some weight in Hyperapp? 🎉 

Most new apps won't need SSR/hydration initially, and those that will are the more sophisticated users on larger projects that probably won't mind adding a small function to do this in userland:
```js
const hydrate = element => {
  const hydrateNode = node =>
    node && {
      name: node.nodeName.toLowerCase(),
      props: {},
      children: [...node.childNodes].map(
        child =>
          child.nodeType === Node.TEXT_NODE
            ? child.nodeValue
            : hydrateNode(child)
      )
    }
  return hydrateNode(element.children[0])
}
...
container = document.getElementById("app")

app(state, actions, view, container, hydrate(container))
...
```

Adding a new optional argument isn't a breaking change (although this would be easier with the old object props instead of spread out), and I considering removing hydration from core more of a performance change since the initial `patch` will handle a nullish `oldNode` perfectly fine by creating all new elements.

This saves 57 bytes in the process.

issue.title: Expansion Country Individual Account Permissions
issue.body:
# Goal
Create interface to display and manipulate permissions set up on [backend](https://github.com/Tiny-Hands/tinyhands/issues/372).

# Details
- Country list should get populated by the country table
- Once country is selected (other than all), station list should be visible and populated by station table (filtering only those associated with selected country)
- Update should be required on each page instead of allowing user to switch between permission type (IRF/VIF/Budget, etc.) and location while requiring front-end to keep track of changes.
- Permissions should cascade down. If user has budget add permission for "Nepal" "All" then when selecting "Nepal" "Birgunj", the budget add permission should be shown.
- Controller should receive a list containing all of the users permissions along with all countries and all stations so that when changing values in the locations drop downs, the user's permissions for that permission group/location would be displayed.

# Questions
- Related to cascading permissions, should removing a permission at a more granular level be disabled? (i.e. If a user has budget add permission for all of Nepal, should removing it for a specific station in Nepal be disabled?)
- Should general account info (email, first/last name, designation) be it's own tab/permission group instead of  a constant part of the page?
- Should permissions have a "granularity" attribute whereby you could decide whether or not a permission can be controlled at a country or station level? For example, the email notifications would only need to go down to a country-based level and allowing station-based granularity would add some unnecessary complications for the permission-checking on that feature. Budget permissions would be another set of permissions that wouldn't require station-specific access. (This affects front & back-end)
# Pictures

#### User with all IRF permission for all countries
![account1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7903547/34432312-4603bb86-ec9e-11e7-8511-b0428544dd4e.png)

#### User with view and add permission for single station in Nepal

#### User with view permission for all stations in Nepal. 
In this case even though the "All Nepal" IRF add permission says no, because the user has IRF add permission for a specific station in Nepal, they would be able to enter IRFs for that station.

Convert []interface{} to []string from plugins (#66)

Convert []interface{} from plugins to []string if appropriate.

add support for indexes (#70)

add support for indexes

resolves #2
This commit introduces new fields to the Table template object that
expose index information. This information includes the database name
of the index (Name) and the Columns used in the index. 

The MySQL implementation uses a generated table
(information_schema.STATISTICS).

The Postgres implementation uses a handwritten SQL query, much like
other functions in database/drivers/postgres/parse.go.

check for public schema before trimming table name (#76)

resolves #75

In Postgres, calling ::regclass on a table OID will prefix that table
with the schema if the table exists outside of the search path.
Practically speaking, that means any table outside of "public".

introduce new funcs to ForeignKeyColumns (#81)

These funcs retrieve the list of DBNames for the ForeignKey's columns
and referenced columns. This allows one to do things like:
```
{{ range .RefTable.Columns.DBNames.Except .FKColumns.RefColumnDBNames }}
```

* add column names funcs to ForeignKeyColumns
* fix broken foreign key anchors

ensure consistent index ordering (#83)

* ensure consistent index ordering

fixes #82

The databases return index data in a consistent order. The previous
process did not respect that through its use of a map as an
intermediate store. By using slices, we now guarantee that the template
will see the indexes in the order the database returned them.

* pluralize tableIndex

expose column comments (#85)

expose column comments

resolves #77

This commit exposes comments that have been attached to columns in the
DB.

surface index uniqueness (#88)

resolves #87

Uniqueness is a basic, but important, bit of information for an index.
This information has been available from the DB but it was never
surfaced.

pull_request.body:
- Fixed NOT operator, that didn't work because it assumed that the variables were 32 bit wide and the variables were actually 64 bit wide.
- Removed custom types (`SLONG`, etc) and some C types occurrences by `stdint.h` types (`int32_t`, etc).
- Renamed `PI` to `M_PI`.

This fixes https://github.com/rednex/rgbds/issues/212

issue.body:
I get this error after about 3 minutes of running rollup. (usually my bundle is created in 1.6 seconds!). 

What I am trying to do is add into the bundle either CESIUMJS or millsymbol.js

- https://cesiumjs.org/downloads/
- https://www.spatialillusions.com/milsymbol/docs/index.html

in npm speak, I added them as:

npm  install cesium --save
npm install milsymbol --save

Currently include them in the project via <script> tags 

```
      <script src="../node_modules/cesium/Build/Cesium/Cesium.js"></script>
      <script src="../node_modules/milsymbol/dist/milsymbol.js"></script>
```
I would like to add them in my rollup bundle directly. with:
```
import Cesium from 'Cesium'
import milsymbol from 'milsymbol'
```

or if it is needed:
```
import Cesium from 'cesium/Build/Cesium/Cesium.js'
```

Here is how I added the commonjs and resolve plugins to my rollup.config.js (which works for all the other local src code and css files).

```
import resolve from 'rollup-plugin-node-resolve'
import commonjs from 'rollup-plugin-commonjs'
import minify from 'rollup-plugin-minify-es'
import postcss from 'rollup-plugin-postcss'
import cssnano from 'cssnano'

export default {
    input: 'scripts/Main.js',
    output: {
        file: 'dist/bundle.js',
        format: 'es',
        sourcemap: 'inline'
    },
    plugins: [
        resolve({
            jsnext: true,
            main: true,
            browser: true,
        }),
        postcss({
            plugins: [cssnano()],
            extensions: ['.css'],
        }),
        commonjs(),
        minify()

issue.title: could Synergy fit on a floppy?
issue.body:
Even today the floppies are still being used, for example - as virtual floppies inside the coreboot open source BIOS. Just imagine: your wonderful OS could be a part of someone's BIOS build! _(for coreboot supported motherboard, maybe you have or could get one - see https://www.coreboot.org/Supported_Motherboards )_

If you already have a coreboot-supported motherboard, or a real chance to get one, - wouldn't it be cool to be able to launch your own OS straight from the BIOS chip? ;) With one simple command its possible to add any floppy to coreboot BIOS build - and then you see it as a boot entry! Multiple floppies could be added this way _(as long as you have enough space left inside the BIOS flash chip, luckily LZMA compression could be used for the stored floppies to reduce their occupied size)_

issue.title: .coafile: Fix ignore files field not created
issue.body:
duplicate the generator ignore_globs as it was getting exhausted, all_files was already disjoint from ignore_globs, corrected condition

1.)  `ignore` globs is a `generator object`. If you iterate through it once, it gets exhausted. I found 2 instances where the same exhausted object was being used to iterate through over again i.e. the second time it wasn't going inside the loop, so what I did was duplicated that generator object using `itertools.tee()` and for one iteration send `ignore_globs_backup` and for the second used `ignore_globs`

2.)  This condition https://github.com/coala/coala-quickstart/blob/50b358a60454932c0c33fe9443f305abd1103b11/coala_quickstart/generation/Settings.py#L64 will always be false because of the line https://github.com/coala/coala-quickstart/blob/50b358a60454932c0c33fe9443f305abd1103b11/coala_quickstart/generation/Settings.py#L58 NOTE: while setting the value of `all_files`, `ignore_globs` is passed to the `collect_files` function. The `not` had to be removed from this condition, but it was decreasing code coverage.

3.)  I wrote an extra test case to increase code coverage since there wasn't any test case which was actually passing any thing to `ignore_globs`

Closes #157

issue.title: Debian packaging in progress
issue.body:
Hi!

This is a friendly notice to let you know that [Debian](https://debian.org/) is working on packaging your software for Debian. You can follow the progress of that work in [bug #867800](https://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=867802) in the Debian Bug Tracking System (BTS).

The source code for the Debian package is in [this git repository](https://anonscm.debian.org/cgit/python-modules/packages/rawkit.git/). It will be uploaded into Debian shortly, at which point it will end up in the [NEW queue](https://ftp-master.debian.org/new.html) for legal review. Once the NEW process is completed, it takes about 10 days for the package to trickle down into "testing", which will become the next Debian release. This means your software will eventually be shipped in a "long term support" release, which last from three to five years, according to the [current statistics](https://wiki.debian.org/DebianReleases#Production_Releases).

If you are interested in maintaining the package yourself upstream, that is definitely possible. You can either upload the package yourself if you are a Debian member or I can act as a sponsor when a new release is published.

This is just a notification, but can also act as a coordination point for upstream packaging if you wish to followup on this. otherwise, feel free to close this issue whenever you like.

issue.title: ci: use commitlint to validate messages
issue.body:
This change picks up on the description in this commit: https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/dff6ee3

> Ideally we should switch over to something like https://www.npmjs.com/package/commitplease
as suggested in #9953 but that package currently doesn't support strict scope checking,
which is one of the primarily goal of this PR.

As commitlint is a specialized tool that includes strict scope checking as mentioned in the commit, I thought it might be desirable to replace the tooling code with less complex tool usage.

There is no issue with the current implementation aside from being a non-trivial amount of code. This does not change the current commit validation behaviour.

## PR Checklist
Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit
- [ ] ~~Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)~~
- [ ] ~~Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)~~


## PR Type
What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->
```
[ ] Bugfix
[ ] Feature
[ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
[ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
[ ] Build related changes
[x] CI related changes
[ ] Documentation content changes
[ ] angular.io application / infrastructure changes
[ ] Other... Please describe:
```

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?
```
[ ] Yes
[x] No
```

## Other information

* Picks up on comments in angular/angular#dff6ee3
* Replaces project-internal tooling
* Motivated by commitlint/commitlint#119

issue.title: 2014 general election precinct results
issue.body:
You'll find 2014 results files you'll be converting in town-specific files in the [CT sources repository](https://github.com/openelections/openelections-sources-ct). Many of these are either PDFs or Excel files. For electronic PDFs, we recommend using [Tabula](http://tabula.technology/), which is free, to extract data. The goal is to create a single CSV file for each town, with the following headers:

`county`, `precinct`, `office`, `district`, `party`, `candidate`, `votes`

For the following offices: Governor, Treasurer, Comptroller, Attorney General, Secretary of State, U.S. House, State Senate, State House. issue.title: Digitrax Command Station OpSw programming via roster
issue.body:
Provides Digitrax Command Station OpSw programming support and command station "decoder" definitions for Digitrax command stations, via "Roster Entry" and the symbolic programmer.  This mechanism could potentially replace the tool at "LocoNet->Configure Command Station" tool.

Programming is via the "service-mode" programmer using the new "Command Station Op Switches" mode.

Adds the new programming mode to the Digitrax programming mechanism in `SlotManager`.

XML definitions for DCS5x, DB150, DCSx00, and DCS210/DCS240 are included.

comment.body:
@rhwood,

Good inputs!  Will take care of the first item and second item, no question.

I've struggled some with "hiding panes".  Seems like I managed click the "hide unpopulated sheets" preference for the programmer part-way thru development.  Will attempt to hide "function labels", and anything else which happens to show up.  

Any future development which adds "defaulted" panels will also have to be handled.  Unless I can figure out a way to have a "decoder" definition which is not based on an "mobile" decoder.  More research to do...

I expect to have difficulty disabling the "function labels" sheet.  I haven't noticed a "decoder" which successfully gets rid of it - for example the NCE "Light-it", RR-CirKits "Towerman", CML "DAC20", ...

I have no idea how to get rid of the "Function Labels" sheet!  Adding a pane with the same tab name doesn't replace it; I get the same old sheet plus an additional "Funcion Labels" sheet.  It appears to be created automatically via JAVA, rather than being specified in XML.  It shows up for every other "non-mobile" decoder definition I've looked at - NCE 'Light-it', CML 'DAC20', RR-CirKits 'TowerMan', DigiRails 'DR4018', and others.  Do you have any specific recommendations?

I intentionally placed the OpSws in the "OpSws" sheet, instead of the "CVs" sheet.  OpSws are NOT CVs, and cannot be programmed on the service-mode programming track.  This is a decision of "semantics" which plays out as an attempt to not confuse the user (while providing possible confusion).  If I could get the column header on the CVs table to say "OpSw" instead of "CV", I would, but I believe that is again coded in the `.properties` file, so it cannot be overridden.

pull_request.title: Update a bunch (225+) of homepages (permanent redirect problems as found by repology)
pull_request.body:
###### Motivation for this change

This is my effort for #30636, well, a first blast at trying to fix the easy issues.

The repository was passed through a script, specific version used available here:

 * https://github.com/samueldr/repology-autofixer/commit/1730c627bc0a28990072aadc9836cf882ad1ad3c

It has changed *mostly* meta homepage URLs, **BUT**, some download URLs have been changed. This is a side-effect of the dumb (but effective) way the change is handled. All download URLs that were a sub-path of the homepages have been automatically converted. For all URLs changed, this happened to be http→https.

###### Things done

*Nothing was tested*, no build of any of the affected software was done as this is all metadata changes.

The commits have been viewed (with my eyeballs) one by one. I have checked a couple of them manually to see whether all was right or not, especially when download URLs were changed too. If something fails, it's likely that it is the download URL, and that download URL already was previously failing.

YES, if anything fails, (except for URLs having disappeared), I'll take responsibility and *clean it through the script*.

* * *

Last, I would like to know if there's already some guidelines for commits made with automated tools. This is the way my commits look (the quote quotes the problem as stated in repology):

```
zeal: Updates homepage URL.

This commit automatically fixes the following problem:

> Homepage link "http://zealdocs.org/" is a permanent redirect to
> "https://zealdocs.org/" and should be updated

(Commit automatically made using repology-autofixer)
```

If there is anything you would like added or changed to the messages, just ask, running this script is *really cheap*, it's basically one API request, and some (short) waiting time.

I wanted to see if I could setup Drone on my laptop to get a feel for the system. I found http://docs.drone.io/installation/ and tried to follow the instructions there.

The instructions are not very precise and assumes a lot of familiarity with docker-compose. I had heard of docker-compose in the abstract, but here I needed to look at the help to figure out that I need to name the config file `docker-compose.yaml`. I've created #283 to improve this.

Actually running `docker-compose up` doesn't work then. You get lots of errors about undefined variables. So I kept reading and saw that the rest of the page slowly "patches" the configuration to get it nearer a working state (but doesn't actually end up giving me a working configuration).

Next confusing point was the integration with version control providers. Sure, I thought, it's nice if I can configure Drone to checkout my GitHub repositories. It's not clear that the provider is really used as an OAuth provider — #284 tries to address this.

These were some initial stumbling blocks I ran into. My next question is if it's even possible to run Drone on a laptop for testing purposes. The use of OAuth and the rediction URL makes me wonder this — I would set it to `localhost/authorize`, but will that work?

The lack of confidence is a problem — ideally, the installation guide would be a step-by-step guide that quickly shows me how to get Drone running on my laptop. _If_ registration with third parties is absolutely necessary, then this should be shown in a step-by-step way too.

Right now, the installation instructions seem like a sketch at best. It might be that they really are just a sketch and that there are plans for expanding them. If that's the case, please write a note at the top saying so :-)

comment.body:
Feel free to close this issue if it's not helpful. I guess what I'm asking for is for the Drone project to consider

* What state do you expect the user to be in after reading the installation overview? Should I have a local Drone server up and running? If so, I believe the document needs more detailed step-by-step instructions.

issue.title: could Tachyon fit on a floppy?
issue.body:
Even today the floppies are still being used, for example - as virtual floppies inside the coreboot open source BIOS. Just imagine: your wonderful OS could be a part of someone's BIOS build! _(for coreboot supported motherboard, maybe you have or could get one - see https://www.coreboot.org/Supported_Motherboards )_

If you already have a coreboot-supported motherboard, or a real chance to get one, - wouldn't it be cool to be able to launch your own OS straight from the BIOS chip? ;) With one simple command its possible to add any floppy to coreboot BIOS build - and then you see it as a boot entry! Multiple floppies could be added this way _(as long as you have enough space left inside the BIOS flash chip, luckily LZMA compression could be used for the stored floppies to reduce their occupied size)_

issue.title: PtrDiff between pointers generate DIV with 1
issue.body:
**Version Used**: 
VS 15.5.2

**Steps to Reproduce**:
During our work in the Cosmos AOT compiler we had encountered this function used in UTF8Encoding class:
https://github.com/dotnet/coreclr/blob/master/src/mscorlib/shared/System/Text/UTF8Encoding.cs#L794

it seems that there is a problem in the optimization of this code as the IL generated is this:

```
IL_0000: nop
IL_0001: ldarg.0
IL_0002: ldarg.1
IL_0003: sub
IL_0004: ldc.i4.1
IL_0005: div
IL_0006: conv.i8
IL_0007: conv.u4
IL_0008: ldc.i4.1
IL_0009: shr.un
IL_000a: stloc.0
IL_000b: br.s IL_000d
IL_000d: ldloc.0
IL_000e: ret
```

ILSPY decompile this IL in C# in this way that makes no sense:

```cs
private unsafe static int PtrDiff(char* a, char* b)
{
    return (int)((uint)((long)((a - b) / 1 * 2)) >> 1);
}
```

That is not the hyper optimized code that this complicated casting wanted to obtain...

**Expected Behavior**:
No DIV by 1 should be present

**Actual Behavior**:
DIV by 1 is present

comment.body: It is code part of CoreRT so I imagine it has been compiled with optimizations enabled.

For mapping symbols to operations you can do the following: 
```js
const operators = {
 '*' : (a,b) => a * b,
 '+' : (a,b) => a + b,
 '-' : (a,b) => a - b,
 '/' : (a,b) => a / b,
 '**': (a,b) => a ** b
}
```

Then, you can check if something is an operator using `Object.keys(operators).includes(operator)`.

And you can do operations using `stack.push(operators[operator](parseFloat(b),parseFloat(a)));`.

issue.title: monerod using tons of bandwidth after 100% synced blockchain
issue.body:
Monero 'Helium Hydra' (v0.11.1.0-release)

Reproducibility: always

Steps:
Have monerod running with blockchain already 100% synced.

What happened:
monerod constantly uses tons of bandwidth.

Expected result:
monerod uses minimal bandwidth since the blockchain is already synced. There shouldn't be need for such massive use of bandwidth after the blockchain has synced.

Notes:
Looks like monerod uses some kind of P2P functionality to seed the blockchain to other nodes that have not yet synced to help propagate the blockchain. But why the need for such massive use of bandwidth? This forces me to shut down the daemon as soon as I quit the app. zcashd for example uses minimal bandwidth so I basically keep it running 24/7 without even noticing the bandwidth use.

comment.body:
Just as a reference for the next person looking to manually limit the rate in the GUI, the following commands are available.

```
  --limit-rate-up arg (=-1)             set limit-rate-up [kB/s]
  --limit-rate-down arg (=-1)           set limit-rate-down [kB/s]
  --limit-rate arg (=-1)                set limit-rate [kB/s]

issue.title: README lists unsupported configuration flags
issue.body:
The `README` lists the following sample configuration:
```xml
<configuration>
  <includeStale>false</includeStale>
  <maxWidth>160</maxWidth>
  <sortImports>NO</sortImports>
  <javadocFormatter>NONE</javadocFormatter>
  <style>GOOGLE</style>
  <filterModified>true</filterModified>
  <skip>false</skip>
</configuration>
```

However, the options `maxWidth`, `sortImports` and `javadocFormatter` are no longer supported. Do you plan to reintroduce these?

comment.body: Ack. Unfortunate, but it is what it is. I filed #7 so that all you have to do is press a button :).

issue.title: Ooze shield with small brim or skirt attached
issue.body:
Since an ooze shield is only a single line wide there are times when it will not stay attached to the bed very well.  It is catching a lot of ooze strings and can easily get ripped off the bed.

I turn on the skirt with a distance of 2 and 4 lines to create a "Brim" that the ooze shield connects to to keep it on the bed better.  This only works on the outside shields.  Inside shields don't get a skirt attached.

If I turn on a full brim as a workaround it gets attached to the object as well which I'm trying to avoid.

If an ooze shield could automatically have the bottom layer be 4 lines thick (or user selectable?) to the outside of it (side away from the object) this would make it much easier to set it up and have it stick well.

comment.body:
It still works with the brim.

Improving the ooze shield adhesion on inside by attaching it to the skirt was just removed from our planning by our project manager because it was older than 12 weeks.

pull_request.title: LED Blink
pull_request.body:
This is a simple project to make an LED repetitively blink.

Requires: x1 Arduino Board, x1 Breadboard, x1 5mm LED Light, x2 Jumper Wires, x1 220, 1K, or 10K resistor.

Steps:
1. Place the positive jumper wire into digital port 13, with the other end being in the positive node of the breadboard.
2. Place the negative jumper wire into digital port GND, with the other end being in the negative node of the breadboard.
3. Place your LED with the positive wire being in the main area of the breadboard, and the negative wire on the negative node of the breadboard.
4. Place your transistor on the positive node of the breadboard, with the other end being in the same row as your LED. Be sure not to make them touch!
5. Plug in your Arduino and run the program.

issue.title: Incompatibility between embed proxying and X-Frames: SAMEORIGIN
issue.body:
I'm having a display issue where embeds frames from Wordpress won't show in my feed because Wordpress itself uses a frame whose headers comprises `X-Frames: SAMEORIGIN`. This means the browser won't load the frame if the parent frame isn't the same exact domain. Normally, it should always work, as the parent embed URL is supposed to be on the same Wordpress domain. Except with Friendica proxy feature. Since we proxy the embed URL through the Friendica domain, the browser enforces the policy and don't display the frame. Example: Original post with WP embed: https://friendica.mrpetovan.com/display/735a2029185a48fca2c460a319316270 Working embed URL: https://blog.mrpetovan.com/slice-of-life/2017-holiday-road-trip-florida-new-orleans/embed/ Non-working proxy URL: https://friendica.mrpetovan.com/oembed/aHR0cHM6Ly9ibG9nLm1ycGV0b3Zhbi5jb20vc2xpY2Utb2YtbGlmZS8yMDE3LWhvbGlkYXktcm9hZC10cmlwLWZsb3JpZGEtbmV3LW9ybGVhbnMv Wordpress embed URL code: ````html
A (Mostly) Sunny Holiday Road-Trip Through Florida To New Orleans
```` The solution is simple on paper: stop proxying WordPress embeds. However, detecting WordPress wouldn't be trivial, or it would have to be manually by domain, which would be cumbersome. The last resort could be to disable proxy for all embeds, but then the browser's Mixed Content policy would kick in and refuse to display non-https embeds. Or maybe just proxying non-http embeds that can be identified just on the URL alone? What do you think?

comment.body: The proxy is also a way to disable tracking attempts.

- Legacy ID: 542

Related programs: [Share KM](https://sites.google.com/site/droidskm/) ([Android app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.liveov.skm&hl=en))

> What is the problem you wish to solve?  
> Control the Android interface via input-device on network-connected host  
> 
> What is your new feature idea?  
> Port or build of the Synergy client (synergyc) for the Android OS  
> 
> Is there already a less convenient way?  
> No; not that I'm aware of  
> 
> How useful would the feature be to others?  
> Extremely.  
> Will vastly improve Android's appeal & versatility.  

It would be extremely valuable to be able to control the Android mobile from HID's; definitely keyboard, mouse would be nice.  
Taking hands off keyboad & mouse (which may already be controlling numerous systems), to "fiddle" with mobile device or Android MID disrupts productivity flow/pace.  
Entering values, such as strong passwords on small mobiles with compound keyboard is also overly time-consuming, that could be done quickly & easily with a standard keyboard.  

Since Android is also POSIX-based (Linux kernel derivative), it would seem "simple" to rebuild the source the the new architecture, but unfortunately this is beyond my own skill-set.  

[NOTE: this may be a possible duplicate of an existing thread @ "https://code.google.com/p/synergy-plus/issues/detail?id=57":https://code.google.com/p/synergy-plus/issues/detail?id=57 ]

issue.title: cleaning printfs and error handling
issue.body:
In `op_hdf5.c` there were inconsistencies how to print log information and how to handle errors.

* replacing all `printf(...)` with `op_printf(...)`.
* replacing all `return NULL` with `exit(2)`.
* put some `if (OP_diags > ...) {}`around log-prints`.

The last point helped in getting nicer log-files when fetching `op_dat` directly to h5-container.

pull_request.title: Removes ATOM/BOND_SPTR in boost::graph in favor of raw pointers
pull_request.body:
This removes the boost::shared_ptr usage in the boost graph.  It greatly reduces the memory footprint of a molecule and has a nice performance boost as well (at least on OS X).

Some more testing is required with valgrind to make sure it doesn't leak.

We may also consider making the lifetime of deleted atoms and bonds the lifespan of the molecule container to help prevent certain classes of issues when using the wrapped interfaces.

Started base Framework for Team system

The team system will work based on three operating teams and one spectator team. The three operating teams are the Class D, Foundation, and SCP teams. Team Class D will be tasked with getting as many of their own out of the building as possible. Team Foundation will be tasked with containing the breach (Killing Class-Ds and returning SCPs to containment). Team SCP will be tasked with killing as many people as possible.

Removes automatic app image creation.

This has nothing do with the quality of the code provided by probonopd;
this change is due to the fact that I barely maintain LoS anymore and
therefore want to minimize infrastructure that could break. Automatically creating and
providing binaries for different platforms might be a feature again some day, but in
a more standardized manner when I build the infrastructure for all my
projects, not just LoS.
